reuse.why: Adds a new worstCaseAmount in shared/rules instead of changing the existing shared/schedules getScheduledAmount, which already handles missing, single and ranged amounts and is used by the client.

duplication.why: Every server site keeps its own missing/number/range dispatch around the new helper, and getScheduledAmount still carries a separate (midpoint) definition of the same rule.

placement.why: A schedule amount rule is placed in shared/rules.ts (rule-condition utilities) while the schedule amount helper lives in shared/schedules.ts.

scope.why: Only the range computations, a new helper with tests and a release note are touched.

maintainability.why: The rule now has two definitions that disagree: server sites use worstCaseAmount, while getScheduledAmount (client balances and schedule tables) and the schedule preview in shared/schedules.ts still use the midpoint.

bypasses_abstraction.where: forecast-schedules.ts, schedules/app.ts (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule) and schedule-template.ts call worstCaseAmount inside their own dispatch instead of getScheduledAmount (shared/schedules.ts).

disguised_duplication.where: The per-site `amount == null ? 0 : typeof amount === 'number' ? amount : ...` dispatch is kept at each site with only the range branch swapped, duplicating getScheduledAmount's structure under a new range helper.

one_place.where: worstCaseAmount (shared/rules.ts) serves four server sites, but getScheduledAmount and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions in shared/schedules.ts still use the midpoint, and each site still decides the missing/single cases itself.
